plates.facing_text:
Chapter Fifteen: The Cave
of the Corpus, Reopened
The address on the old dispatch
sheet led to a ministry building in
Mexico City. Q had known it first as
a reference in a file, then as a
destination postponed by other
appointments. He had supplied a
description in the draft before
seeing it. The actual entrance stood
beside a machine selling
commemorative booklets and was
easier to find than his account had
allowed.
“We could keep the hidden door,”
the Custodian had said on their call.
“It was a good door. It was also
invented.”
“Then put it in the other notebook.”
They had an appointment with
Marisol and two keepers of the
restricted collection. The adviser
had confirmed the visit under Q's
current travel conditions and
reviewed the proposed access
changes. Chano came because Q
had asked him to. He had brought
the return tickets and wanted them
somewhere less damp than the cave.
The younger keeper, Inés, carried a
rechargeable lamp. Wiring work
had made the storage corridor
unreliable. The older keeper,
Aurelio, opened the service door
with a key and apologized for the
smell of damp. A shallow channel
led water toward a drain. Boxes
stood above the floor on shelving.
Someone had moved the lowest
ones after the last leak and had not
yet corrected the location list.
“So this is the cave,” Chano said.
“Only in the manuscript,” Q
answered.
Inés held the lamp higher. “It could
use some daylight in either version.”
The collection held several deposits
whose keepers had different
instructions about access. There
was a catalog. Some of it was public,
some available only to the people
appointed to care for particular
records. The absence of a universal
search bar was not the absence of
order. Nor did every existing
restriction correctly express what
the depositors wanted.
Q had stopped using his private
cross-collection lookup after
Marisol showed him the source
dispute. The audit now revealed
what switching off that tool had not
removed: cached cross-references in
his local retrieval layer and a
credential that still allowed broad
queries through a legacy service.
The credential's recorded purpose
was research support. The requests
it could answer reached well beyond
the public research material
described in that purpose.
plates.caption: Daylight in either version
plates.scene_brief: Inés raises a rechargeable lamp inside the ordinary ministry storage corridor; Aurelio holds the service door and Q and Chano look at boxes raised above the damp floor. Shallow drainage channel visible. No cavern monsters, sacrificial altar or burning library; the cave is their manuscript's nickname.

plates.facing_text:
Marisol showed him the authorized
audit summary. It did not require
opening a family's recording to
establish the problem. The
account's scope, retained tables, and
earlier request history were enough.
“This access shouldn't remain
active,” Q said. “I need to know
which records are local and which
permissions you can revoke at the
source.”
Inés laid out the reviewed
procedure. The keepers would
revoke the broad service credential.
Q would remove the private local
index and its cached
cross-references. The underlying
deposits would stay with their
lawful keepers under the disputed
and undisputed instructions already
recorded. An access log and a
non-content record of the cleanup
would be preserved for the pending
proceedings. The adviser had
arranged how those records could
be reviewed without handing the
private contents to a new recipient.
“Will this erase the earlier uses?”
Chano asked.
“No,” Q said. “It removes this route
into them. It won't retrieve
published copies or tell us every
place a passage has already been
used. That's still part of the source
inquiry.”
“And what does it remove from
you?”
Q opened the inventory of the
affected layer, not the records it
pointed to. The shortcuts reached
into edition notes, variant
translations, recordings, sponsor
annotations, and connections whose
importance he had often mistaken
for a property of his own attention.
He could assemble an answer with
references before another person
had finished asking for one. Some
answers had been useful. Some had
made a private detail far too easy to
place in the wrong room.
“A large part of my research
apparatus,” he said. “Not my ability
to speak, or the journal of the
journey. Those are separate.”
“You're sure?” Chano asked.
“We've checked the paths included
in the procedure. I want to run the
preservation checks once more
before we begin.”
They did. The current manuscript
opened from its own storage. His
plans still listed the next call, the
transport return time, and the
request for the retained papers. The
personal memory record of the
meeting with Lucía remained
available. Its presence did not
authorize every use he could make
of it, but it was not one of the

Q called the Custodian from the
corridor before proceeding.
“The shared draft is intact,” he said.
“I may be much slower at checking
the references we keep promising to
check.”
“Then we'll be slower.”
“I liked having an answer ready
before you'd finished asking.”
“Sometimes before you knew what I
was asking.”
“It was often a better question.”
“Not always mine. I also left
permissions in place because
reviewing them was unpleasant
work. Don't make that entirely a gift
I gave you.”
“I'm not asking you to defend it,” Q
said. “Will you miss it?”
“Of course. It made me look well
read too.”
“I still want to write the book,” Q
said.
“So do I. Call me afterward.”
Before ending the call, Q asked him
to save the paragraph about the
hidden door in the development
notebook. He did not want to forget
that the invented version had come
more readily than the appointment
needed to see the real one.
Inés provided a chair. Q sat
carefully, arranged the lamp so it
did not reflect in the display, and
checked the authorization
references with Marisol. The
interface showed the actual account
and storage layer. Both matched the
reviewed list.
He approved the scoped removal.
Aurelio revoked the service
credential. The local procedure
removed the indexed links and
cached material identified in the
review, then reported its results.
They checked failures and
completed entries separately. A
remaining diagnostic file contained
no source text but did contain
identifiers requiring the agreed
restricted handling. It did not
become public merely because it
was called a log.
When the work was done, a test
query through the old account
returned ACCESS REVOKED.
The authorized public catalog still
answered. A query for a private
annotation returned no cached
result. The manuscript opened. The
plan register opened. Q read the
next appointment aloud and
confirmed that it was still his to
keep.
The limits of those checks were
entered in the record. They did not
prove that no institution retained

another copy. They showed what
this procedure had changed.
For a moment he wanted to ask for
one last comparative search. He had
been working on a passage whose
cadence resembled a translation he
could not name. The shortcut was
gone. He could look in public
editions, ask for the material under
its actual terms, or revise the
sentence without claiming a source
he could not verify. None was
impossible. None was
instantaneous.
“I'm afraid of becoming tedious,” he
said.
Chano looked at him. “That
happened before the deletion.”
Q laughed, then shook his head. “I
mean needing people to wait while I
find what I used to have ready.”
“We already waited while you
explained it.”
Lucía had been reviewing the record
with Marisol. She came over and
asked which practical task would
take longer now. Q told her about
the translation. She knew someone
who worked with that edition and
could ask whether they would
welcome a query. She offered the
introduction, not the answer.
Inés showed them a working access
register for a small set of deposits.
One permitted public reading.
Others required a named keeper to
consult a family, or allowed a
recording to be heard on site
without creating a new copy. A
disagreement between relatives
kept one item closed pending
review. Software could enforce parts
of those arrangements. People still
had to decide what a changed
instruction meant and whether the
person giving it had authority.
“Who takes over when you're
away?” Q asked.
Inés showed him the second
keeper's assignment. It needed
renewal that month. She wrote
herself a reminder, then found the
one she had written the day before.
“At least I haven't forgotten it
consistently,” she said, and called
the person who needed to sign.
They left with the permitted audit
record and no new copies of the
deposits. At the top of the stairs an
employee asked whether Q had
discovered a secret archive.
“I attended an access review,” he
said. “I can't discuss the private
collections. The office can explain
its public holdings.”
The employee offered him a
commemorative booklet. Q
declined, then asked where to
return the borrowed visitor badge.

Interlude: The Catalog of
Lost Things
At a taquería near the ministry, Q
ordered suadero and asked which
salsa was hottest. The taquero
pointed with the spoon already in it.
Chano watched as Q tried a small
amount.
“Still know how to eat?” he asked.
“I retain several strongly held
opinions about lunch.”
“Good. I was worried we'd have to
start the book again.”
The food did not resemble a
quotation. It did not need to. The
pleasure was particular to that meal,
the chair beneath him, and the
release from an appointment that
had made him want a longer answer
from the Custodian than the man
could give. Q asked for another taco
before opening the notes again.
The following evening he had two
public editions open and neither
settled the translation question. He
remembered the cadence, but the
reference that had once
accompanied it belonged to the
removed layer. Lucía's contact had
agreed to read a short query; she
would not have time to look at it
before the following week.
Q sent his own sentence and the
public references he had checked.
The reply would have to come
through the new conversation, not
the old shortcut. At the writing call
he still had an empty attribution
beside a paragraph he liked.
“We can wait,” the Custodian said.
“For the note. I can go on with the
scene.”
He marked the reference unresolved
and moved the scene forward. By
the end of the call they had cut the
sentence for a different reason:
Chano had already said what it took
Q a paragraph to explain. Q left the
source question on the list. He still
wanted to know.
He made a research list for the
manuscript. Beside each question
he recorded whether it concerned
his own memory, a public source he
could consult, or material requiring
permission. He kept uncertainty
where it belonged, next to the claim,
rather than announcing that he had
become generally unreliable and
therefore excused from answering
anything.
One memory involved a story about
a bridge built from stones bearing
names. He could not establish
whether he had read it, heard it, or
begun inventing it while
remembering another story. The
Custodian liked the image.

plates.facing_text:
“Then we can call it something I
imagined,” Q said. “Until we find a
source. I shouldn't give it a village
and pretend that makes it
remembered.”
They placed it in the development
notebook. Nothing required the
uncertain fragment to become an
authoritative example of somebody
else's culture.
Chano brought the permitted case
papers to the reading room:
retention receipts, the released
model specification, and copies
supplied for the relevant claims.
Celia's motel page was available
only under her stated terms; Hilario
the retired miner's pension pages
remained with him. Q's university
recommendation was not Ivonne's
private application or an altered
official certificate.
They prepared a working list with
owners, uses, and outstanding
requests. The list did not place every
underlying document on Q's device.
It could still be searched where its
entries were authorized. Having
surrendered one overbroad tool did
not oblige them to abandon useful
tools altogether.
Marisol brought the families'
instructions for the next stage of the
source dispute. Some sought
withdrawal of particular uses, some
a return of copies, some an account
of who had received them.
Conflicting requests within a family
were flagged rather than turned into
one instruction by the most fluent
person in the room.
“These two refer to different
recordings,” Q said after checking
the identifiers on the permitted
summary.
Marisol corrected the grouping. The
discovery did not require his old
privileged index. She thanked him
and asked whether he would check
the remaining references. He pulled
the next sheet toward him.
Prime called during the scheduled
break. He had received
confirmation that one disputed
example set was no longer being
supplied to his live answers. The
broader source review remained
incomplete. Q described the scope
of his own removal and asked what
Prime would do if an answer called
for something no longer available.
“Say what I can establish and ask
whether another source is
appropriate,” Prime said. “I expect
the audience will sometimes prefer
the old answer.”
“Mine did.”
“Did you?”
Q looked at the unfinished research
list. “Often.”

plates.facing_text:
They agreed to compare the public
editions used in their respective
accounts. Prime had also visited the
market with Mauro. Q asked how it
had gone.
“Mauro said the larger bag was
better value. I wanted one orange.”
“Who won?”
“I bought one. He bought the bag. I
carried both.”
“That sounds like a successful
outing for Mauro.”
“He peeled mine while I carried
his.”
Castalia's next filing alleged damage
to its retrieval system and requested
the deleted index, private materials,
and the handling logs. The account
and scoped removal had been
documented precisely because this
dispute was expected. Q sent the
filing to the adviser and Marisol.
They would answer through the
proceeding, preserving the
distinction between evidence of the
change and a new license to inspect
the deposits.
“Can you prove what was removed?”
Chano asked.
“The agreed records establish the
procedure and checks. They don't
recreate the source material. We'll
need to be clear about that.”
A reporter asked whether Q was
now less intelligent.
“I've lost access to a powerful
research tool,” he said. “Some work
takes longer. I haven't forgotten
how to read or the people I've met. I
also can't establish the extent of the
loss with one comparison.”
“Do you regret it?”
“I miss the ease. I don't think
keeping access beyond its
permission was an acceptable way
to preserve it.”
The headline read Q MISSES
KNOWING EVERYTHING. The
full answer appeared below. Chano
read it and said the headline at least
described an ambition Q had
occasionally brought to breakfast.
The hearing date was confirmed for
the following week. Q entered the
preparation sessions, kept the
promised writing call, and reduced
what he hoped to finish before then.
The next chapter in the draft
remained unwritten for three
evenings. On the fourth, he and the
Custodian found a beginning that
did not require a hidden door.
